Application Materials.content:
You will need to provide the following documentation as part of your application. This list of documents may vary slightly from course to course.
- **Academic qualifications:** Please provide a transcript for your degree study. If you have not yet completed your degree please provide a transcript of your results achieved to date. If you have completed more than one university qualification, please provide a transcript and certificate for both.
- If your degree was awarded by a UK university, please upload a transcript of your marks for each year or an electronic Higher Education Achievement Reports (HEAR).
- If your degree was awarded by an overseas institution, you should supply a transcript of your marks for each year of your studies and a copy of your degree certificate together with a certified translation if the document is not in English. International and EU applicants are also advised to include high school transcripts.
- We accept copies of physical transcripts and degree certificates as well as electronic transcripts and certificates. Please **do not** submit originals of certificates or transcripts by post.
- If you are submitting copies of physical documents, you should upload to your application clear, colour photographs or scans of your original qualification documents (not copies or certified copies). These documents must confirm that the qualification has been awarded, show the date of the award, and show the final awarded grade.
- **Referee details:** Please provide the contact details of one or two referees on your application as required. You should provide details of an academic referee if you are currently studying, or if you have graduated within the last five years. Professional references may be considered if you have graduated more than five years ago.
- Open references will normally only be accepted if they are written on headed paper, provided as a colour copy of the original, and provide the referee’s work contact details. If you have open references, please upload these at the time of application.
- If you do not have open reference, Queen Mary will contact your referee(s) via email to supply a reference, preferably electronically. References sent by email must be sent from a university or company email address; references from a personal email address such as 'Yahoo' or 'Hotmail' are not acceptable.
- Paper reference forms should be endorsed by an appropriate institution/company stamp or on official institution/company letterhead, and should be provided as a scanned colour copy of the original.
- **Statement of purpose:** Your statement of purpose should explain why you want to study your chosen programme and how it will help your future career aspirations. This should typically be one side of A4 paper.
- **Curriculum Vitae (CV)/Resume**
- **English language certificate (if applicable):** If English is not your first language, you should provide evidence of English language ability: IELTS, TOEFL, or other acceptable proof. See the [English Language Requirements](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/international-students/englishlanguagerequirements/) section for more details.
- You can still apply even if you haven't yet received your final transcript or your Certificate of English proficiency. You will receive a conditional offer stating what qualifications and grades you will need to achieve; once you have evidence of obtaining your qualifications you can upload them to the MySIS Applicant portal.
- Some postgraduate programmes may require applicants to have submitted their Reference letters before a decision has been made.

Application Deadlines.content:
Dates and deadlines apply to courses delivered on site at Queen Mary University of London. Some programmes have specific application deadlines; if no deadline is specified then the below deadlines will apply.

- **January 2027 entry:** Deadline for postgraduate Overseas applications is **Monday 14th December 2026**. Welcome week is **Monday 18th - Friday 22nd January 2027**; teaching begins **Monday 25th January 2027**.

Academic Requirements.content:
- UK applicants: **A good 2:2 (55% or above) or above** at undergraduate level in a subject with substantial mathematical content, including Mathematics, Statistics, Physics, Engineering, Economics and Computer Science.
- China applicants: Queen Mary normally considers a **Bachelor Degree (minimum 4 years) from selected institutions** for entry to postgraduate taught programmes. For a UK 2:2 degree equivalency: **65 to 75%**. Offer conditions will vary depending on the institution you are applying from.
- You do not need to be a programming expert.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
The English Language requirements for entry to postgraduate taught and research programmes in the School of Mathematics falls within the following English band: **Band 4: IELTS (Academic) minimum score 6.5 overall with 6.0 in each of Writing, Listening, Reading and Speaking**.
Queen Mary accepts a range of English tests and qualifications categorised in its English bands to demonstrate English Language proficiency. See [all accepted English tests](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/international-students/englishlanguagerequirements/accepted-english-language-tests-and-qualifications/) deemed equivalent to these IELTS scores.

Program Overview.content:
Data Analytics MSc is part of Mathematical Sciences and AI, Computer and Data Science at Queen Mary University of London. In today's data-driven economy, organisations need data experts to extract clear insights and inform decision making. This masters teaches the core mathematical principles of data analysis and AI, and how to apply these to real-world scenarios, while developing programming, machine learning and visualisation skills. Students build a foundation in mathematics and statistics, work with Python and R, apply learning to real-world datasets from a wide variety of sectors, learn from experienced educators including industry practitioners and Fellows of the Alan Turing Institute for Data Science and AI, and choose their own specialism.
Study options include full-time study starting September 2026 for 1 year, part-time study starting September 2026 for 2 years, and full-time study starting September 2027 for 1 year. The location is Mile End.
In the first semester, students complete compulsory modules that provide a foundation in data analytics, machine learning, and the statistics of data analysis, building on this knowledge with industry-standard tools and software. In the second semester, students decide on a specialism, also known as a stream, designed to prepare them for specific career paths. Streams include Applied Machine Learning, Pattern Recognition and Deep Learning, and Statistical Inference. Over the summer in the third semester, students work alongside one of the programme's researchers on an independent research project to consolidate learning and develop applied data science skills. Students do not need to be programming experts and will explore data analysis tools such as R and Python.
Assessment is 67% modules and 33% research project. Students are assessed by a mixture of formal examinations and coursework in taught modules and undertake more self-directed work in completing the final Data Analytics Project.
Teaching is primarily through lectures and tutorials, alongside independent study and research. Students are assigned an Academic Adviser who will guide them throughout their time at Queen Mary.
Programme-related teaching and faculty include Dr Alexander Shestopaloff, Senior Lecturer in Statistics, whose interests include efficient Markov Chain Monte Carlo methods, high-dimensional time series analysis, network science, online Bayesian learning and empirical market microstructure; Professor Mark Jerrum, Professor of Mathematics, whose research interests include combinatorics, computational complexity, stochastic processes and randomised algorithms; Professor Vito Latora, Professor of Applied Mathematics and Chair of Complex Systems, with expertise in complex systems and complex networks; Dr Melania Nica, Reader in Actuarial Science and Programme Director for MSc Actuarial Science and Data Analytics, whose research interests include finance and insurance based on application of economic theory; and Dr Nicola Perra, Reader in Applied Mathematics and Programme Director for MSc Data Analytics, whose research focuses on human dynamics, data analytics, network science, mathematical and digital epidemiology.
Facilities include the recently refurbished, £18m Mathematical Sciences building with high-quality teaching rooms, private and group study areas and a social hub; a shared office and dedicated computer lab with Bloomberg terminals for MSc students; library access to 8,000 mathematical books and subscriptions to mathematical journals; and on-campus accommodation for all new full-time postgraduate students from outside London. Teaching is based at Queen Mary's main [Mile End campus](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/about/howtofindus/mileend/), one of the largest self-contained residential campuses in the capital, 15 minutes by tube from Central London.
Students who have graduated from this programme have gone into data analysis, data science and software development roles including Data Science Consultant, AI Scientist, Pricing Analyst, Customer Insights Analyst, Senior Product Data Analyst, APP Development Specialist, Quantitative Risk Analyst and Market Risk Analyst. Recent employers include British Airways, Ocado, Accenture, PwC, KPMG, UBS, BlackRock, London Stock Exchange Group, Canary Wharf Group, Tata Consultancy Services and Bloomberg.

Curriculum.content:
Programme Structure: the MSc Data Analytics programme is structured across three semesters. In the first semester, students complete compulsory modules that provide a foundation in data analytics, machine learning, and the statistics of data analysis, working with industry-standard tools and software. In the second semester, students decide on a specialism/stream. In the third semester, over the summer, students work alongside one of the School’s researchers on an independent research project.
Semester A compulsory modules:
- Machine Learning with Python
- Probability and Statistics for Data Analysis
- Storing, Manipulating and Visualising Data
- Programming in Python
Semester B streams:
- Applied Machine Learning: two compulsory modules, Computational Statistics with R and Forecasting with AI; choose two elective modules from Bayesian Statistics, SAS for Business Intelligence, Optimisation for Business Processes, Financial Data Analytics, and Digital and Real Asset Analytics.
- Pattern Recognition and Deep Learning: two compulsory modules, Neural Networks and Deep Learning and Advanced Machine Learning; choose two elective modules from Graphs and Networks, Forecasting with AI, Bayesian Statistics, and Computational Statistics with R.
- Statistical Inference: two compulsory modules, Bayesian Statistics and Computational Statistics with R; choose two elective modules from Graphs and Networks, Neural Networks and Deep Learning, Forecasting with AI, and Advanced Machine Learning.
Data Analytics Project and Dissertation: Each Data Analytics MSc student is required to complete a **60 credit project dissertation**. A typical MSc project dissertation consists of about 30 word-processed pages, covering a specific research-level topic in data analytics, usually requiring the student to understand, explain and elaborate on results from one or more journal articles and/or performing computation, simulations, or analysis. Possible areas include time series analysis, exploratory data analysis on a dataset, performance and comparative analysis of state of the art techniques, theoretical models of data, complex systems, dynamical systems, topological data analysis, experimental design with data, and statistical aspects of data analytics techniques.

Financial Aid.content: Queen Mary is pleased to offer a number of generous scholarships to students on our MSc programmes. A wide range of other scholarships and bursaries are available, including the [Queen Mary Alumni Loyalty Award](http://www.qmul.ac.uk/postgraduate/taught/funding_masters/queen-mary-alumni-loyalty-award/) and the UK government's international [Chevening Awards](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/scholarships/items/chevening-awards.html). **Find out about all scholarships and bursaries available to Queen Mary postgraduate applicants [here](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/postgraduate/taught/funding_masters/).** If you have any questions about Scholarships available to applicants within the School of Mathematical Sciences, please contact [maths@qmul.ac.uk](mailto:maths@qmul.ac.uk).

Multiple Applications.content:
You may apply for a maximum of **two taught programmes** or **one taught and one research programme** at Queen Mary per application cycle. You can only study for one qualification at a time, so if you receive offers for both programmes you will be required to accept one and decline the other.
Is there an application fee? No, the university does not charge an application fee.

Deferral Admission Policy.content: The withdrawal and deferral process differs depending on your programme level and your enrolment status. If you were accepted through Clearing then you cannot defer and will need to decline your offer and apply via the main application cycle. Deferral deadlines are published online for [Postgraduate Taught](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/postgraduate/taught/deadlines/) programmes, and the [Enrolment FAQs](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/newstudents/faqs/enrolment/) set out the withdrawal and deferral processes in more detail.

Conditional Admission Policy.content: You can still apply even if you haven't yet received your final transcript or your Certificate of English proficiency. You will receive a **conditional offer** which will state what qualifications and grades you will need to achieve in order to meet Queen Mary's entry requirements. Once you have received evidence of obtaining your qualifications you can upload them to the [MySIS Applicant portal](https://mysis.qmul.ac.uk/), after which you will receive an unconditional offer once all conditions have been met.
